interpretation: C has a small positive finite mean SeamCov difference versus A (+0.0698235 percentage points), not zero improvement. Its median is negative, only3/8 parents improve, and the mean remains below START; it fails the registered +5pp/6of8 screen.

B and D mean SeamCov are lower than A. D interaction for SeamCov is negative; it does not demonstrate a useful additive combination. Other metrics have different signs and must not be described as universal harm.

All four continued arms improve mean global free squared-distance quality versus START, but all lose mean SeamCov versus START. Better free reconstruction alone does not satisfy the attachment objective.
C has a robust severe exposure loss on parent f59627a077dcc2566c63b8b48495261a versus START; its bound is above10percentage points. This is not resolved by small reference-visibility uncertainty.

P1 supports retaining START as the maintained baseline for this attachment objective, while preserving all endpoints as evidence. This does not claim START is universally best in quality or all local metrics.
